views.name: race_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time
FROM races

params.description: A normalized, one-row-per-race view exposing basic race attributes and scheduled session datetimes (practice, qualifying, sprint).
params.when_to_use: List or lookup of races and their metadata (id, year, round, circuit, name, url). | Joining race-level attributes into analyses where one row per race is required (e.g., season calendars, circuit-level summaries when joined appropriately). | Displaying or exporting race schedule information (dates and times for FP1/FP2/FP3/qualifying/sprint).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need aggregated race-related metrics computed from related many-row tables (for example, counts, totals or averages from race_results, pit_stops, or laps). This view is strictly one row per race and contains no aggregates; joining it to many-row tables without re-aggregation will produce row multiplication and mis-counts. | Do not use as a source of driver- or constructor-level measures. driver- or constructor-level metrics live in driver_dim, constructor_dim, race_results_w_driver_constructor, driver_lap_summary, etc.; joining those without correct grouping/cohorting can cause incorrect metrics. | Do not use to compute event-level time series metrics that require event ordering inferred from other tables (for instance, fastest-lap ranks or running points). Those are available in race_fastest_lap_rank, driver_running_points_by_season, latest_driver_standing_per_season, etc.
params.output_schema: race_id: Unique identifier for the race. Source: races.race_id | year: Season year in which the race took place. Source: races.year | round: Championship round number (string/number as stored) within the season. Source: races.round | circuit_id: Foreign key referencing the circuit hosting the race. Source: races.circuit_id | name: Official race name. Source: races.name | date: Official race date (typically the main event date). Source: races.date | time: Official race start time (as stored). Source: races.time | url: Reference URL for the race (info/page). Source: races.url | fp1_date: First practice session date. Source: races.fp1_date | fp1_time: First practice session time. Source: races.fp1_time | fp2_date: Second practice session date. Source: races.fp2_date | fp2_time: Second practice session time. Source: races.fp2_time | fp3_date: Third practice session date. Source: races.fp3_date | fp3_time: Third practice session time. Source: races.fp3_time | quali_date: Qualifying session date. Source: races.quali_date | quali_time: Qualifying session time. Source: races.quali_time | sprint_date: Sprint session date (if applicable). Source: races.sprint_date | sprint_time: Sprint session time (if applicable). Source: races.sprint_time
params.grounded_columns: races.race_id | races.year | races.round | races.circuit_id | races.name | races.date | races.time | races.url | races.fp1_date | races.fp1_time | races.fp2_date | races.fp2_time | races.fp3_date | races.fp3_time | races.quali_date | races.quali_time | races.sprint_date | races.sprint_time
params.metric: No derived aggregates or computed metrics in this view. All output columns are direct projections of base table columns (identity mapping). Example formalization: race_id = races.race_id (no aggregate).
params.composition: Safe to join (cardinality-safe) to dimension/lookups that are one-to-one or many-to-one from races using circuit_id or year — for example: join to circuit dimension on races.circuit_id = circuit_dim.circuit_id because each race references a single circuit (one row in race matches one row in circuit), so race-level rows and attributes are preserved without duplication. | Safe to join to season-level dimension tables keyed by year (e.g., season_dim on year) because races.year is one value per race and season_dim has one row per year. | Do NOT join directly to tables/views that are one-to-many from races without first aggregating or otherwise controlling cardinality, because that will multiply race rows and silently corrupt measures. Examples of one-to-many targets to avoid joining raw: race_results_w_driver_constructor (many drivers per race), driver_lap_summary (many drivers/laps per race), pit_stops_per_driver (multiple pit stops per driver per race), qualifying_grid_with_driver (multiple grid entries per race), race_fastest_lap_rank (multiple ranked laps per race). If you must combine, join using a pre-aggregated subquery keyed by race_id (for example, aggregated_counts AS (SELECT race_id, COUNT(*) AS entrants FROM race_results GROUP BY race_id) JOIN aggregated_counts USING (race_id)), so that race row cardinality remains one-to-one. | When composing with joins that include driver or constructor dimensions, prefer joining through explicit keys (driver_id or constructor_id) on aggregated race-level measures originating elsewhere, not by joining race -> results -> driver_dim directly without aggregation, which would expand the race grain.
params.comparison: Use race_results_w_driver_constructor instead when you need per-race per-driver or per-constructor results and associated measures (positions, points, status). race_basic has only race-level metadata and will not contain driver results. | Use driver_lap_summary or race_fastest_lap_rank when you need lap-level or fastest-lap ranking metrics. Those sibling views are aggregated or ranked on lap/driver and include computed measures that race_basic lacks. | Use pit_stops_per_driver when you need pit stop counts/durations by driver in a race. pit_stops_per_driver contains per-driver aggregated pit metrics; joining it directly to race_basic would multiply race rows unless pit_stops_per_driver is aggregated to race level first. | Use qualifying_grid_with_driver when you need qualifying grid position and driver details; that view is at the driver-by-race grain and will produce many rows per race, unlike race_basic's one row per race.

views.description: Normalized race rows with canonical typed date/time and key descriptive columns. Use this as the canonical race dimension for joins and time-based filters. | Use for: List races by year/round/date; Join races to results/pit_stops/qualifying; Filter races that had a sprint or specific session

views.name: driver_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers

params.description: A normalized dimension of drivers: one row per driver with identifying attributes and reference metadata.
params.when_to_use: Lookup driver attributes (name, date of birth, nationality, URL) by driver_id or driver_ref. | Enrich event- or result-level rows with stable driver attributes prior to aggregation. | Join to facts that are already at driver-level (e.g., driver season aggregates) to add descriptive fields.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining directly to this view when you need to aggregate driver-related events (races, laps, pit stops) without re-aggregating — it will not cause duplication itself, but joining a one-row-per-driver dimension to a one-to-many fact is fine; the anti-pattern is: joining a many-row fact (race_results, pit_stops, laps) to another many-row fact through this view expecting deduplication. WHY: driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, so it does not prevent many-to-many inflation between two fact tables; you must aggregate or join via shared keys at the correct grain. | Using this view as a source of measures or aggregates (e.g., counting drivers per season) when the driving truth is in an event/fact table. WHY: it contains only descriptive columns and no temporal/seasonal keys — counts derived here are of drivers overall, not season-specific cohorts. | Assuming driver_dim contains season-specific or race-specific attributes (e.g., number used in a particular season). WHY: number and code here are driver-level attributes as stored in the drivers table, not contextual values that can change by season or race.
params.output_schema: driver_id: unique surrogate/int identifier for a driver (source: drivers.driver_id) | driver_ref: external/reference string for the driver (source: drivers.driver_ref) | number: driver race number (driver-level attribute, source: drivers.number) | code: short driver code (driver-level attribute, source: drivers.code) | forename: driver's given name (source: drivers.forename) | surname: driver's family name (source: drivers.surname) | dob: driver's date of birth (source: drivers.dob) | nationality: driver's nationality as stored in the drivers table (source: drivers.nationality) | url: link to driver's profile page (source: drivers.url)
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driver_id | drivers.driver_ref | drivers.number | drivers.code | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.dob | drivers.nationality | drivers.url
params.metric: This view exposes no aggregates or derived metrics. All columns are direct projections from base columns in the drivers table. | No derived_col = <aggregate/expression> definitions are present in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_w_driver_constructor on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver and race_results_w_driver_constructor is a fact keyed to driver_id; enriching the race_result rows with driver attributes will not duplicate the race results. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_grid_with_driver on driver_id — safe for the same reason: driver_dim is a dimension, one row per driver, so it won't multiply qualifying rows. | do NOT join driver_dim to driver_lap_summary or pit_stops_per_driver expecting to merge their measures without considering grain — those are aggregated at driver+(race|lap) grain. While joining is safe (won't duplicate rows from the dimension side), you must be careful when combining multiple different driver-level aggregates from separate aggregated views: if they are aggregated at different grains (e.g., per race vs per season), joining them directly can produce incorrect cohorts or double-counting unless you align/aggregate to a common grain first. | do NOT join this view to other many-to-many facts to perform deduplication across facts. Example anti-pattern: joining race_results -> driver_dim -> pit_stops_per_driver and assuming unique result rows — the join to driver_dim does not resolve duplication between race_results and pit_stops_per_driver; you must join facts via shared keys (race_id + driver_id) or pre-aggregate appropriately. | Safe to join to constructor_dim on constructor_id via an intermediate fact (race_results_w_driver_constructor) — driver_dim itself has no constructor key, so joining driver_dim directly to constructor_dim would be meaningless; instead join both dims to the fact to preserve cardinality.
params.comparison: use race_basic instead when you need race-level context (race date, circuit, season) along with driver attributes — race_basic provides event-level fields that driver_dim does not contain. | use constructor_dim instead when you need constructor attributes rather than driver attributes — constructor_dim has constructor-level metadata while driver_dim has person-level metadata. | use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need driver performance per race or to combine driver and constructor measures — that view is a join/fact combining driver, race, and constructor context while driver_dim only provides descriptive attributes. | use driver_lap_summary or pit_stops_per_driver when you need aggregated performance metrics (lap times, pit counts) — those are aggregation views containing measures; driver_dim contains no measures. | use driver_season_points or driver_running_points_by_season when you need season-scoped points/cohort metrics — those views have season keys and aggregated points, which driver_dim does not provide. | use latest_driver_standing_per_season or race_fastest_lap_rank when you need ranked or windowed standings — those sibling views contain window/rank logic and season/race context absent from driver_dim.

views.description: Canonical driver dimension preserving identifiers and name parts for joins and display. Use when queries need driver attributes or to join driver events. | Use for: Look up driver names/nationality/age; Join drivers to results, lap_times, pit_stops, standings

views.name: constructor_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructor_id,
  constructor_ref,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors

params.description: A normalized dimension of constructors (teams) providing one row per constructor with identifiers and basic attributes.
params.when_to_use: Lookup constructor attributes (name, reference code, nationality, URL) when you need constructor metadata keyed by constructor_id. | Join to fact tables (race results, race, qualifying, pit stops) to attach constructor descriptive fields without changing aggregation results. | Build reports or dashboards that filter or group by constructor identity or display constructor details.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to a one-to-many fact without joining on the fact's grain (e.g., races or results) and then aggregating — doing so can cause row-multiplication in the result set if you expect one row per constructor but the fact has multiple rows per constructor (grain mismatch). | Using this to compute constructor-level aggregates (points, laps, pit stop counts) — this view contains no measures or aggregates, so using it alone for metrics will be wrong (it provides attributes only). | Assuming this view is cohort-aware or time-aware — it is a static snapshot of constructors from the base table and does not represent changes over time or season-scoped memberships; aggregating across seasons using only this view will produce silently incorrect cohort results. | Joining to another dimension that is not one-to-one (if such exists) under the assumption of preserving counts — if the join partner has multiple rows per constructor_id, you must aggregate the partner first or the join will multiply rows.
params.output_schema: constructor_id: Unique identifier for the constructor (team). Source: constructors.constructor_id | constructor_ref: Short reference code for the constructor. Source: constructors.constructor_ref | name: Full name of the constructor (team name). Source: constructors.name | nationality: Nationality of the constructor as recorded in constructors.nationality | url: External or metadata URL for the constructor. Source: constructors.url
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or other views on constructor_id (e.g., race_results_w_driver_constructor ON constructor_id) — safe when the target side is the fact and you intend to preserve each fact row's multiplicity; this dimension itself is one-row-per-constructor so it will not duplicate its own rows. | Join to driver_dim (if needed) on nothing — there is no direct relationship; do NOT expect a one-to-one relation between constructors and drivers unless you pre-aggregate by constructor in the driver-side view. | Do NOT join this view to a one-to-many view (e.g., race_results_w_driver_constructor, qualifying_grid_with_driver, pit_stops_per_driver) with the intent of keeping one row per constructor without first aggregating the many-side to constructor-level totals — such joins will multiply constructor rows by the many-side cardinality and will cause mis-counted aggregates. | If you need constructor-level aggregates from multi-row sources (race_results_w_driver_constructor, driver_season_points, pit_stops_per_driver, driver_lap_summary), first aggregate those sources grouped by constructor_id, then join the aggregated result to constructor_dim on constructor_id to avoid duplication. | Safe to join to other one-row-per-entity dimensions like driver_dim only when you have a valid one-to-one key relationship and you intend to widen attributes; verify keys before assuming one-to-one.
params.comparison: use race_basic instead when you need race-level attributes or the race grain — race_basic provides race-specific fields, while constructor_dim is only constructor metadata. | use driver_dim instead when you need driver metadata — driver_dim is the analogous dimension for drivers; do not conflate driver and constructor attributes. | use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need combined facts of races, drivers and constructors (results-level rows and measures) — that view contains the many-side measures and the join context necessary for per-result analyses, whereas constructor_dim only supplies descriptive attributes. | use driver_season_points or driver_lap_summary when you need aggregated metrics (points, laps) — those sibling AGG views contain computed metrics; constructor_dim contains no aggregates.

views.description: Canonical constructor/team dimension preserving identifiers and descriptive attributes for joins. | Use for: List constructor names/nationalities; Join constructors to results/standings

views.name: race_results_w_driver_constructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.constructor_id,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.position_text,
  r.position_order,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.rank,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.status_id,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  d.number AS number__driver,
  c.name AS name,
  c.constructor_ref
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON r.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON r.constructor_id = c.constructor_id

params.description: Row-level results for each race result enriched with driver and constructor attributes (one row per result_id).
params.when_to_use: Look up detailed fields for a specific race result (by result_id) including driver name/code and constructor name/ref. | List all results for a race (race_id) with driver and constructor attributes while preserving the native result-level granularity. | Join result-level attributes into another dataset when you need exactly one row per result and can tolerate missing driver/constructor attributes (LEFT JOIN semantics).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to compute aggregated metrics across results (e.g., total points per driver or per constructor) without first aggregating by the correct key — this view is at the result_id grain so summing points here is valid only if you intentionally want the sum of points of the included result rows; using it as if it were pre-aggregated by driver or by race will silently overcount. | Do not join this view directly to a driver-level or constructor-level aggregated view expecting no duplication if that other view is one-row-per-driver/constructor-per-season: if the target aggregation expects to absorb multiple results per driver, you must aggregate results first to the matching grain. Otherwise you will create a fan-out (many results per driver) and accidental multiplication when subsequently aggregating. | Do not treat driver identification via number__driver (drivers.number) as the primary key for deduplication — drivers may change numbers or have nulls; rely on driver_id (this view exposes driver_id). | Avoid using this view to compute event-level summaries (e.g., number of laps in a race) because laps here are per-result and summing can double-count if the same laps metric is repeated across joined rows; use a race-level view (race_basic) for race-level single-valued fields.
params.output_schema: result_id: Unique identifier for this result row, derives from results.result_id | race_id: Foreign key to the race, derives from results.race_id | driver_id: Foreign key to the driver, derives from results.driver_id | constructor_id: Foreign key to the constructor, derives from results.constructor_id | number: Competitor number as stored on the result row, derives from results.number | grid: Grid position for the start, derives from results.grid | position: Finishing position text/number as stored in results.position (same as position_text for some datasets), derives from results.position | position_text: Textual finishing position (could be 'R', 'DNF', etc.), derives from results.position_text | position_order: Integer ordering of finishing position used for sorting, derives from results.position_order | points: Points awarded for this result, derives from results.points | laps: Number of laps completed by this result, derives from results.laps | time: Formatted race time string for this result, derives from results.time | milliseconds: Time in milliseconds for this result, derives from results.milliseconds | fastest_lap: Fastest lap number set by this result (if any), derives from results.fastest_lap | rank: Championship or session rank value as stored on results.rank, derives from results.rank | fastest_lap_time: Formatted fastest lap time string for this result, derives from results.fastest_lap_time | fastest_lap_speed: Speed recorded for fastest lap for this result, derives from results.fastest_lap_speed | status_id: Foreign key to status table indicating result status, derives from results.status_id | forename: Driver given name, derives from drivers.forename (LEFT JOIN drivers ON results.driver_id = drivers.driver_id) | surname: Driver family name, derives from drivers.surname | code: Driver short code, derives from drivers.code | number__driver: Driver table's number field (drivers.number) — may differ from results.number and can be NULL | name: Constructor name, derives from constructors.name (LEFT JOIN constructors ON results.constructor_id = constructors.constructor_id) | constructor_ref: Constructor short reference, derives from constructors.constructor_ref
params.grounded_columns: results.result_id | results.race_id | results.driver_id | results.constructor_id | results.number | results.grid | results.position | results.position_text | results.position_order | results.points | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.fastest_lap | results.rank | results.fastest_lap_time | results.fastest_lap_speed | results.status_id | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.code | drivers.number | constructors.name | constructors.constructor_ref
params.metric: points = results.points  -- atomic measure present at the result_id grain; do not re-interpret as pre-aggregated beyond result rows | laps = results.laps  -- per-result lap count; summing across this view equals total laps across returned result rows (which is usually not a race-level single value) | milliseconds = results.milliseconds  -- per-result time in ms; use aggregate functions explicitly when combining rows (min/avg/sum) depending on analytic intent
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim (or the underlying drivers table) on driver_id using a one-to-one join — safe because drivers is one-row-per driver_id so enriching this view with driver attributes will not duplicate result rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim (or constructors) on constructor_id using a one-to-one join — safe because constructors is one-row-per constructor_id so constructor attributes will not duplicate result rows. | do NOT join this view directly to driver_lap_summary, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid_with_driver, or any other one-to-many-per-result driver/session table without first aggregating that table to result_id (or to the same grain you intend). Those tables are aggregated/partitioned differently (per-driver-per-lap, per-pit-stop, per-qualifying-row) and will multiply result rows and thereby multiply measures like points unless you re-aggregate or restrict the join to a single row per result_id. | do NOT join to driver_season_points or driver_running_points_by_season expecting no duplication — those are aggregated per driver-season (many results map to one driver-season). If you need season totals alongside result rows, aggregate results up to the driver-season grain or use windowed metrics carefully. | If you need to attach a single value from a many-row sibling (e.g., fastest-lap-rank per race), first reduce that sibling to one row per race/result_id (for example, by selecting the minimal rank or limiting to FASTEST_LAP_FLAG) before joining to avoid inflating counts/points.
params.comparison: use race_basic instead when you need race-level singletons (e.g., race date, total laps for the event) rather than per-result metrics — race_basic has race-level grain, this view is result-level. | use driver_dim instead when you only need driver attributes without result-level repetition — driver_dim is one-row-per-driver and avoids duplication when joining to other aggregated datasets. | use constructor_dim instead when you only need constructor attributes without result-level repetition. | use driver_lap_summary, pit_stops_per_driver, or qualifying_grid_with_driver when you need aggregated or session-specific metrics (laps-by-driver, pit stop counts, qualifying times) — those views are aggregated at different grains and provide summary metrics not present on each result row. | use race_fastest_lap_rank or latest_driver_standing_per_season when you need ranked or windowed results (fastest lap ranks, season standings) rather than raw result rows; those sibling views express rank/window semantics which this join view does not compute.

views.description: Denormalized results joined to driver and constructor attributes. One row per result (result_id) with driver/constructor descriptive columns and race key for easy analysis. | Use for: Show finishing positions with driver/constructor names; Compute driver/constructor points per race; Filter results by driver or constructor attributes

views.name: driver_lap_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_milliseconds,
  MIN(lap) AS first_lap,
  MAX(lap) AS last_lap
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.description: Per-race, per-driver lap time summary: counts and basic statistics (min/avg/max) plus first/last lap number for each driver in each race.
params.when_to_use: Calculate how many laps a given driver completed in a specific race and the distribution of their lap times (min/avg/max). | Join per-driver-per-race lap summary to race or driver dimensions to report driver performance summaries at race-level. | Filter drivers by lap_count or by their fastest/slowest lap time within a race.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to a one-to-many table (for example, pit_stops_per_driver or lap_times) without re-aggregation — doing so will duplicate rows and inflate counts/aggregates because this view is aggregated at the (race_id, driver_id) grain while those tables contain multiple rows per (race_id, driver_id). | Using it to compute per-season or per-driver career aggregates without re-aggregating at the season/driver grain — AVG/COUNT here are per-race-per-driver and cannot be averaged across races without weighting by lap_count or re-aggregating raw lap_times. | Treating first_lap/last_lap as chronological session-wide positions rather than numeric min/max of lap numbers — these are computed as MIN(lap)/MAX(lap) across rows in lap_times and not derived from timestamps; using them as timestamps or absolute sequence positions across events would be wrong.
params.output_schema: race_id: the race identifier — derived from lap_times.race_id (GROUP BY key). | driver_id: the driver identifier — derived from lap_times.driver_id (GROUP BY key). | lap_count: number of lap_times rows for this (race_id, driver_id) — derived from COUNT(*) over lap_times rows for the group. | min_milliseconds: fastest lap time (smallest milliseconds) for this driver in this race — derived from MIN(lap_times.milliseconds). | avg_milliseconds: average lap time (arithmetic mean in milliseconds) for this driver in this race — derived from AVG(lap_times.milliseconds). | max_milliseconds: slowest lap time (largest milliseconds) for this driver in this race — derived from MAX(lap_times.milliseconds). | first_lap: smallest lap number recorded for this driver in this race — derived from MIN(lap_times.lap). | last_lap: largest lap number recorded for this driver in this race — derived from MAX(lap_times.lap).
params.metric: lap_count = COUNT(*) -- count of lap_times rows per (race_id, driver_id) | min_milliseconds = MIN(lap_times.milliseconds) -- minimum milliseconds per (race_id, driver_id) | avg_milliseconds = AVG(lap_times.milliseconds) -- arithmetic mean milliseconds per (race_id, driver_id) | max_milliseconds = MAX(lap_times.milliseconds) -- maximum milliseconds per (race_id, driver_id) | first_lap = MIN(lap_times.lap) -- minimum lap number per (race_id, driver_id) | last_lap = MAX(lap_times.lap) -- maximum lap number per (race_id, driver_id)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE: join to race_basic on race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race; joining will not duplicate this view's per-(race_id, driver_id) rows or its measures. | Cardinality-SAFE: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver; joining will not duplicate rows or alter aggregates. | Cardinality-SAFE: join to constructor_dim only if joined via a one-to-one mapping (e.g., through race_results_w_driver_constructor aggregated to one row per driver per race) — direct join on constructor_id is not available in this view, so only safe after a non-duplicating path. | Do NOT join directly to lap_times or pit_stops_per_driver (both are one-to-many relative to this view's grain) without re-aggregating the child table to (race_id, driver_id) first — doing so will multiply lap_count and other aggregates, producing incorrect sums/means. | Do NOT join to qualifying_grid_with_driver or race_results_w_driver_constructor without ensuring those views are reduced to one row per (race_id, driver_id); if those siblings contain multiple rows per driver per race, they will duplicate measures. | If you need season-level metrics, first aggregate this view (or the underlying lap_times) across race_id to the season/driver grain using a weighted aggregation for avg_milliseconds (weight by lap_count) or re-compute from lap_times to avoid averaging averages incorrectly.
params.comparison: use race_results_w_driver_constructor instead when you need finishing position, constructor linkage, or combined race result fields along with lap-derived metrics — race_results_w_driver_constructor is a join that contains race result attributes not present here. | use pit_stops_per_driver instead when you need pit stop counts/times per driver per race — pit_stops_per_driver contains a different one-to-many aggregation (pit stops) and should be joined only after aligning grain. | use qualifying_grid_with_driver when the question is about starting grid positions — qualifying_grid_with_driver provides starting grid info which is unrelated to lap time aggregates here. | use driver_season_points or latest_driver_standing_per_season when you need season-level standings/points — those are already aggregated to season/driver grains and avoid manual cross-race aggregation mistakes. | use lap_times (base table) when you need row-level lap detail, lap timestamps, or to compute custom aggregates (e.g., weighted percentiles or time-on-track) — this view only exposes basic aggregated stats and lap boundaries.

views.description: Per race_id + driver_id aggregated lap-time measures: lap count, min/avg/max milliseconds and best lap (min). Useful for performance summaries per stint/driver in a race. | Use for: Compare driver lap consistency in a race; Find drivers with fastest single-lap in a race; Filter for drivers who completed a minimum number of laps

views.name: pit_stops_per_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_pit_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.description: Per-race, per-driver aggregated summary of pit stop counts and pit stop duration statistics.
params.when_to_use: You need the number of pit stops a driver made in a specific race (race_id, driver_id) along with average, minimum, and maximum pit stop duration in milliseconds. | Feeding per-driver-per-race pit stop metrics into models or reports that expect one row per (race_id, driver_id). | Joining driver- or race-level attributes (e.g., driver name, race date) to pit stop metrics while preserving the per-race-per-driver grain.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to lower-grain tables (e.g., pit_stops) directly and then aggregating again without re-aggregation — this can double-count pit_stop_count and distort aggregates because pit_stops is the source of these metrics and is one-to-many relative to this view. | Using this view as if it were one-row-per-driver (across seasons) or one-row-per-race only. Its grain is (race_id, driver_id); aggregating without grouping by those keys (or re-aggregating intentionally) will produce cohort-level miscounts. | Expecting event-level details (timestamp, stop_reason) — this view collapses all pit_stops for the race+driver into summary metrics, so any analysis needing per-stop detail must query pit_stops directly. | Joining to other one-to-many siblings (e.g., driver_lap_summary, race_results_w_driver_constructor) without using the proper join keys and re-aggregation; such joins can multiply rows and silently inflate/deflate measures if not done at compatible grains.
params.output_schema: race_id: identifier of the race — sourced from pit_stops.race_id and is the grouping key for this row | driver_id: identifier of the driver — sourced from pit_stops.driver_id and is the grouping key for this row | pit_stop_count: COUNT(*) of pit_stops rows for the (race_id, driver_id) grouping — derived from counting pit_stops records | avg_pit_milliseconds: AVG(milliseconds) across all pit_stops for the (race_id, driver_id) grouping — derived from pit_stops.milliseconds | min_pit_milliseconds: MIN(milliseconds) across all pit_stops for the (race_id, driver_id) grouping — derived from pit_stops.milliseconds | max_pit_milliseconds: MAX(milliseconds) across all pit_stops for the (race_id, driver_id) grouping — derived from pit_stops.milliseconds
params.metric: pit_stop_count = COUNT(*) over rows in pit_stops grouped by (pit_stops.race_id, pit_stops.driver_id) | avg_pit_milliseconds = AVG(pit_stops.milliseconds) over rows in pit_stops grouped by (pit_stops.race_id, pit_stops.driver_id) | min_pit_milliseconds = MIN(pit_stops.milliseconds) over rows in pit_stops grouped by (pit_stops.race_id, pit_stops.driver_id) | max_pit_milliseconds = MAX(pit_stops.milliseconds) over rows in pit_stops grouped by (pit_stops.race_id, pit_stops.driver_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driver_id = pit_stops_per_driver.driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, so it will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to race_basic on race_basic.race_id = pit_stops_per_driver.race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race and will not duplicate measures. | DO NOT join directly to pit_stops (the base table) without re-aggregation — pit_stops is one-to-many relative to this view; joining will produce multiple rows per (race_id, driver_id) and will duplicate pit_stop_count and distort averages unless you re-aggregate at the desired grain. | DO NOT join to driver_lap_summary or race_results_w_driver_constructor unless you ensure compatible grain or re-aggregate — those views/tables may be one-to-many relative to (race_id, driver_id) (for example, lap-level summaries are multiple per driver per race) and will multiply rows. If you need combined metrics, either (a) join on (race_id, driver_id) and then re-aggregate measures carefully, or (b) aggregate the other side to (race_id, driver_id) first before joining. | When composing with sibling aggregations: prefer joining only on the exact keys (race_id, driver_id) and avoid joining on higher-level keys (e.g., driver_id alone) without clarifying intended aggregation. If combining with season-level aggregations (driver_season_points), aggregate this view up to the season-level first (via race -> season mapping) before summing counts to avoid mis-counting races.
params.comparison: use race_basic instead when you need race-level attributes or one-row-per-race data — race_basic is one-row-per-race, while this view is one-row-per (race_id, driver_id). | use driver_dim instead when you need static driver attributes (name, nationality) — driver_dim is normalized driver metadata; pit_stops_per_driver provides only pit-stop metrics tied to race+driver. | use driver_lap_summary instead when you need lap-level or lap-aggregated metrics (laps, average lap time) — driver_lap_summary is suited to lap-derived metrics and may have a different grain (for example, per-lap or per-race aggregated differently). | use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need finishing position, points, or constructor join context per race+driver — that view combines race results with driver and constructor info and may include rows for drivers who did not pit; pit_stops_per_driver specifically summarizes pit stop activity only. | use driver_season_points or driver_running_points_by_season when you want season-level point summaries — those are aggregated across races/season; to combine with pit stop totals per season, aggregate this view up to season first (via joining race_basic to get season_id) before joining to season-level views.

views.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per race and driver: number of stops, average and minimum pit milliseconds. Use for pit strategy analysis. | Use for: Compare pit stop counts and durations per driver/race; Identify drivers with unusually long/short pit stops

views.name: qualifying_grid_with_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.name AS name,
  c.constructor_ref
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructor_id = c.constructor_id

params.description: A row-level join of qualifying records to driver and constructor details: returns one row per qualify_id with qualifying times and the linked driver/constructor attributes.
params.when_to_use: Look up qualifying session results for a specific qualify_id, race_id, driver_id, or constructor_id including driver names and constructor name/code. | Build a display/listing of qualifying grid rows for a race (one row per qualifying entry). | Merge qualifying details into a driver- or race-level report when you want the raw qualifying row granularity preserved.
params.when_not_to_use: Aggregate-level analysis (season totals, counts, averages) — this view is at the qualify_id grain, so summing or averaging its rows across races/seasons without explicit aggregation will produce incorrect results. | Joining additional one-to-many event tables (laps, pit stops, race results) directly to this view expecting measures to remain unduplicated — doing so will multiply qualify_id rows and corrupt counts/metrics. | Using it as a driver-season or race-season cohort without first aggregating by driver_id or race_id — the grain mismatch (qualify_id vs. driver-season) will create silently wrong cohorts or over-counts.
params.output_schema: qualify_id: surrogate primary key for each qualifying row; source = qualifying.qualify_id | race_id: identifier of the race this qualifying row belongs to; source = qualifying.race_id | driver_id: identifier of the driver who set the qualifying time; source = qualifying.driver_id | constructor_id: identifier of the constructor/team for this qualifying row; source = qualifying.constructor_id | number: driver race number as recorded for this qualifying entry; source = qualifying.number | position: finishing position in qualifying (grid position); source = qualifying.position | q1: Q1 qualifying time/value for this entry; source = qualifying.q1 | q2: Q2 qualifying time/value for this entry; source = qualifying.q2 | q3: Q3 qualifying time/value for this entry; source = qualifying.q3 | forename: driver's given name; source = drivers.forename | surname: driver's family name; source = drivers.surname | code: short driver code (three-letter); source = drivers.code | name: constructor/team name for this entry; source = constructors.name | constructor_ref: stable constructor reference code; source = constructors.constructor_ref
params.grounded_columns: qualifying.qualify_id | qualifying.race_id | qualifying.driver_id | qualifying.constructor_id | qualifying.number | qualifying.position | qualifying.q1 | qualifying.q2 | qualifying.q3 | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.code | constructors.name | constructors.constructor_ref
params.metric: qualify_id = qualifying.qualify_id | race_id = qualifying.race_id | driver_id = qualifying.driver_id | constructor_id = qualifying.constructor_id | number = qualifying.number | position = qualifying.position | q1 = qualifying.q1 | q2 = qualifying.q2 | q3 = qualifying.q3 | forename = drivers.forename | surname = drivers.surname | code = drivers.code | name = constructors.name | constructor_ref = constructors.constructor_ref
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on qualifying.race_id = race_basic.race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race; adding race attributes will not duplicate qualify rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim (or driver_lap_summary aggregated to driver_id) on driver_id — safe only if the join target is one-row-per-driver (driver_dim is safe). Do NOT join driver_lap_summary directly unless it is pre-aggregated to one row per driver per race, otherwise rows will multiply. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructor_id — safe because constructor_dim is one-row-per-constructor. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many views/tables such as pit_stops_per_driver, race_results_w_driver_constructor, driver_lap_summary, or race_fastest_lap_rank without pre-aggregating or restricting to one row per qualify_id. These are one-to-many relative to qualifying (e.g., many pit stops or laps per driver per race) and will multiply qualify_id rows and corrupt counts/metrics. | If you need aggregated metrics (counts, averages) from one-to-many sources, aggregate those sources to the same grain (qualify_id, driver_id+race_id, or race_id) before joining, or perform the aggregation after the join using DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER as appropriate.
params.comparison: use race_results_w_driver_constructor instead when you need race finishing results and race-specific measures (positions, points) rather than qualifying times — race_results_w_driver_constructor contains race result metrics and may be one-row-per-result, whereas qualifying_grid_with_driver is one-row-per-qualify entry with q1/q2/q3. | use driver_dim when you only need driver attributes (forename, surname, code) without qualifying-specific fields — driver_dim is a normalized dimension for driver-level joins and avoids referencing qualifying. | use constructor_dim when you only need constructor/team attributes and not qualifying times — constructor_dim is the normalized constructor table. | use aggregated views like driver_season_points or driver_lap_summary when you need season- or driver-aggregated metrics (points totals, lap aggregates); those views present pre-aggregated measures at their respective grains, while qualifying_grid_with_driver is raw qualifying-row-level.

views.description: Qualifying entries joined to driver and constructor details, one row per qualify_id (driver in qualifying). Useful to inspect starting grid and qualifying times (q1/q2/q3). | Use for: Show starting grid with driver names and qualifying lap times; Compare qualifying performance vs race results

views.name: driver_season_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ryear AS year,
  driver_id,
  SUM(points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT race_id) AS races_entered
FROM (
  SELECT rs.race_id, ra.year AS ryear, rs.driver_id, rs.points
  FROM results rs
  LEFT JOIN races ra ON rs.race_id = ra.race_id
)
GROUP BY ryear, driver_id

params.description: Per-season totals of championship points and count of distinct races each driver entered, at the grain of one row per (year, driver_id).
params.when_to_use: Compute a driver's total championship points for a particular season (year). | Compare drivers by season-level points or number of races entered. | Join season-level driver metrics to driver or season/dimension tables without changing aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to a race-level or result-level table and then summing its season_points without first preventing duplication — doing so will double-count because those detail rows will replicate the season row (grain mismatch). | Using this view to answer questions at a race-level or single-result-level (e.g., points in a particular race) — it is aggregated to season and will return the same season_points value repeated for each race if naively joined, which is misleading. | Treating races_entered as a count of starts per driver per entry row rather than distinct races — if you join to a table that has multiple rows per race (e.g., pit stops, laps) and then COUNT(*) you will overcount unless you re-aggregate distinct race_id. | Assuming season_points equals official standings/position without checking whether 'points' in results includes all sanctioned points types (this view only sums the results.points column; if other adjustments exist elsewhere they are not applied here).
params.output_schema: year: season year corresponding to races.ra.year (derived from races.year aliased as ryear in the subquery). | driver_id: driver identifier from results.driver_id (directly from results rs.driver_id). | season_points: SUM(points) per (year, driver_id); derived from results.points (SUM(rs.points)). | races_entered: COUNT(DISTINCT race_id) per (year, driver_id); derived from results.race_id (COUNT(DISTINCT rs.race_id)).
params.metric: season_points = SUM(results.points) aggregated at (races.year, results.driver_id) | races_entered = COUNT(DISTINCT results.race_id) aggregated at (races.year, results.driver_id)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, joining will not duplicate season-level measures. | Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic or a season/year-level dimension on year — safe because year is the grouping key here and joining by year (one-row-per-year) will not duplicate measures. | Do NOT join directly to race_results_w_driver_constructor or any race- or result-level view/table without first aggregating that detail up to (year, driver_id) — those are many-to-one to this view and will multiply season_points and races_entered. | Do NOT join to driver_lap_summary, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid_with_driver, or race_fastest_lap_rank without re-aggregation keyed to (year, driver_id) because those views/tables commonly have multiple rows per race or per lap and will duplicate this view's rows or inflate metrics. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., laps, pit stops), either: 1) aggregate that child to (year, driver_id) first, then join; or 2) join and compute metrics from the detail side and not sum this view's season_points directly.
params.comparison: Use driver_running_points_by_season instead when you need a running (cumulative) points series across races within a season — driver_season_points provides only the season total, not per-race cumulative values. | Use latest_driver_standing_per_season when you need final championship standing/position (rank) per season — driver_season_points gives raw summed points and race counts but does not compute standings or tie-breakers. | Use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need race-level results (points by race) or constructor associations per result — that view is result/race-grained while driver_season_points is season-grained.

views.description: Season-to-date points per driver and year aggregated from driver_standings or results. Useful to rank drivers by season points or examine point progression. (Prefer driver_standings table for season snapshots; this aggregate uses results.points as fallback.) | Use for: Rank drivers by season points; Compare driver season totals across years; Find drivers with most race entries in a season

views.name: race_fastest_lap_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_milliseconds,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY MIN(milliseconds) ASC) AS best_lap_rank
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.description: For each race and driver who recorded laps, returns that driver's fastest lap time in milliseconds and the driver's rank for fastest lap within that race.
params.when_to_use: Find the single best lap time per driver within a specific race and compare drivers by their best lap. | Show fastest-lap leaderboard for a given race (rank ordering among drivers by best lap). | Join driver/race attributes (names, teams, season) to the per-race per-driver fastest-lap statistic without changing its granularity.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need per-lap detail (lap-level analyses) — this view has already aggregated lap rows to one row per race_id,driver_id. | Do not use to compute season- or driver-level aggregates across multiple races without re-aggregating — combining rows across races without correct grouping will produce incorrect counts/metrics. | Do not join directly to one-to-many tables (for example, pit_stops_per_driver or lap_times) expecting measures to remain valid — such joins will multiply rows and silently inflate or duplicate the best_lap_milliseconds or break ranking unless you re-aggregate. | Do not use when you need the raw lap_id or which lap_number produced the best time; this view only preserves the value of the best milliseconds and its intra-race rank, not the originating lap row.
params.output_schema: race_id: race identifier — directly from lap_times.race_id, defines the race partition for ranking | driver_id: driver identifier — directly from lap_times.driver_id, identifies the driver for whom the best lap is computed | best_lap_milliseconds: best (minimum) lap time in milliseconds for that driver in that race — derived as MIN(lap_times.milliseconds) across lap rows for that race_id and driver_id | best_lap_rank: rank of the driver's best_lap_milliseconds within the same race — derived via RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY MIN(milliseconds) ASC), ties receive the same rank and will leave gaps in ranking after ties
params.metric: best_lap_milliseconds = MIN(lap_times.milliseconds)  -- aggregate computed per (race_id, driver_id) | best_lap_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY MIN(lap_times.milliseconds) ASC)  -- window ranking over the aggregated per-driver best within each race
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driver_id = race_fastest_lap_rank.driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, so it will not duplicate this view's per-(race_id,driver_id) rows. | Cardinality-safe: join to race_basic on race_basic.race_id = race_fastest_lap_rank.race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race, preserving this view's grain. | Cardinality-unsafe: do NOT join directly to lap_times (or driver_lap_summary) without re-aggregating/ deduplicating, because lap_times is many rows per (race_id,driver_id) and would multiply rows and invalidate best_lap_milliseconds and best_lap_rank. | Cardinality-unsafe: do NOT join directly to pit_stops_per_driver (or any per-driver-per-race one-to-many detail) without first aggregating that table to one row per (race_id,driver_id), because the one-to-many relationship will duplicate this view's measures. | If you need to combine this view with another aggregated view (e.g., driver_season_points), always join on keys that preserve the intended grain (e.g., race_id + driver_id) and re-aggregate after the join when producing higher-level metrics (season totals, averages) to avoid mis-counts.
params.comparison: use driver_lap_summary instead when you need per-driver aggregated lap statistics beyond just the best lap (e.g., average lap time, lap count) — driver_lap_summary likely contains broader aggregated metrics across laps for a driver per race or other grain. | use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need finishing positions, points, or constructor context for drivers in a race — that view contains result-level outcome data (finishing position) rather than fastest-lap aggregates. | use qualifying_grid_with_driver when you need grid positions from qualifying sessions rather than in-race lap performance; qualifying_grid_with_driver is focused on qualifying session results. | use driver_season_points or driver_running_points_by_season when your question is season-level points or standings; those views are aggregated or windowed to the season granularity and are more appropriate for season summaries.

views.description: Per race, rank drivers by their best lap (minimum milliseconds) using lap_times. Exposes best_lap_milliseconds and best_lap_rank to support top-k fastest drivers in a race. | Use for: Find the top-N fastest lap performers per race; Compare best lap ranks to final results

views.name: driver_running_points_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  driver_id,
  race_id,
  race_date,
  points,
  SUM(points) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY race_date, race_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_points
FROM (
  SELECT ra.year, rs.driver_id, rs.race_id, ra.date AS race_date, rs.points
  FROM results rs
  LEFT JOIN races ra ON rs.race_id = ra.race_id
) sub

params.description: Per-driver, per-race racing points and running (cumulative) points within a season (year) ordered by race date.
params.when_to_use: Get the points a driver scored in a specific race and their cumulative season points up to and including that race (partitioned by year). | Produce time-series of a driver's season points progression (ordered by race_date, tie-broken by race_id). | Join to per-race detail (race-level dimensions) when you need both the single-race points and cumulative points at the race-level grain.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to another one-to-many detail (for example laps, pit_stops_per_driver, or any per-driver-per-lap table) without re-aggregating: doing so will multiply rows and therefore duplicate points and cumulative_points, producing inflated sums or incorrect averages. | Using this view to compute season-level aggregates (e.g., total season points per driver) by grouping across race rows in a downstream query that does not re-derive or trust cumulative_points: cumulative_points here is a running total and the final row per driver/year is the season total — aggregating all rows without care will double-count. | Using this view as a driver-season grain source for cohort or time-window analyses that expect exactly one row per driver-year: this view’s grain is year + driver_id + race_id (multiple rows per driver-season).
params.output_schema: year: Season year from races.year (ra.year). | driver_id: Driver identifier from results.driver_id (rs.driver_id). | race_id: Race identifier from results.race_id (rs.race_id). | race_date: Race date (datetime/date) from races.date (ra.date) — used to order races within a season. | points: Points awarded to the driver in that race from results.points (rs.points). | cumulative_points: Running sum of points for that driver within the same year, ordered by race_date, race_id; defined as SUM(points) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY race_date, race_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
params.grounded_columns: results.driver_id | results.race_id | results.points | races.race_id | races.year | races.date
params.metric: points = results.points | cumulative_points = SUM(points) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY race_date, race_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins: join to race_basic on (race_id) — race_basic is one-row-per-race so joining will not duplicate this view's per-race rows. | Cardinality-safe joins: join to driver_dim on (driver_id) — driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, so it preserves this view's grain and does not duplicate measures. | Do NOT join directly to driver_lap_summary, pit_stops_per_driver, or any per-driver-per-lap/per-stop table without aggregation: those are one-to-many relative to this view’s rows and will multiply rows and thus duplicate points and cumulative_points. | Do NOT join to race_results_w_driver_constructor or qualifying_grid_with_driver if those views contain multiple rows per (year, driver_id, race_id) without ensuring uniqueness: joining duplicate result rows will inflate measures. | If you must join to a one-to-many detail (laps, pit stops, etc.) for analysis, first aggregate that detail to the same grain (year, driver_id, race_id) — e.g., SUM(lap_time) or COUNT(pit_stops) per year/driver/race — then join. This prevents multiplying 'points' and 'cumulative_points'. | When joining to ranking views (race_fastest_lap_rank, latest_driver_standing_per_season), ensure the rank view is at a compatible grain (one-row-per-race-per-driver or one-row-per-driver-per-season as intended). If rank is per-season, join only on (year, driver_id) and be aware cumulative_points here is per-race; season-level ranks should compare to the final cumulative_points row or to an aggregate.
params.comparison: Use driver_season_points (AGG) instead when you need one row per driver per season (e.g., final season totals): driver_season_points is aggregated to the driver-season grain and avoids dealing with multiple race rows or running sums. | Use race_results_w_driver_constructor (JOIN) when you need a fuller denormalized result containing constructor info and other result-level columns in a single row; note that race_results_w_driver_constructor may include additional joins/columns not present here. | Use latest_driver_standing_per_season (RANK) when you need season-end standings/ranks rather than an intermediate running total per race. | Use race_basic when you only need race metadata (date, name, circuit) without driver points or cumulative calculations.

views.description: Running (cumulative) points for each driver within a season ordered by race date. Useful to plot championship progression or compute lead changes. Uses races.date to order events. | Use for: Plot driver championship trajectories; Compute when a driver clinched the championship (downstream filter by cumulative points)

views.name: latest_driver_standing_per_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ds.driver_standings_id,
  ds.race_id,
  ra.year,
  ds.driver_id,
  ds.points,
  ds.position,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ra.year, ds.driver_id ORDER BY ds.race_id DESC) AS rn
FROM driver_standings ds
LEFT JOIN races ra ON ds.race_id = ra.race_id

params.description: Provides the latest driver standing row per driver for each season (year) by ranking driver_standings rows per driver and year with ROW_NUMBER ordered by race_id descending.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the most recent standing (points and position) for each driver within a season (year) as of the last race included in driver_standings. | Filter to rn = 1 to get the latest per (year, driver_id) snapshot for downstream joins or reporting. | Compare driver end-of-season points across drivers when the latest per-season snapshot is required rather than every race-level standing.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view and assuming it is already aggregated to season-level without filtering rn = 1 — if you do not filter by rn = 1 you'll get multiple rows per driver-year (one per race) and produce over-count/duplicate measures. | Using this view to compute season totals by summing points across its rows without first restricting to rn = 1 — points are repeated per race and summing will over-count. | Treating race_id as a season identifier — race_id is a race-level key; the season is represented by ra.year. Aggregations by year should use year and proper deduplication (rn = 1) to avoid cohort/grain errors. | Joining it directly to a one-to-many fact (e.g., lap-level, pit_stops_per_driver) without aggregating the one-to-many first — such a join multiplies the standing row and will inflate measures.
params.output_schema: driver_standings_id: surrogate key of the driver_standings record (source: driver_standings.driver_standings_id). Represents the unique row in the driver_standings table used to rank/latest selection. | race_id: race identifier for the driver_standings row (source: driver_standings.race_id). Used to order standings chronologically within a season; higher race_id means later race in the season in this SQL. | year: calendar season year of the race (source: races.year). Defines the season/cohort partition used by the ROW_NUMBER window. | driver_id: driver identifier (source: driver_standings.driver_id). The subject being ranked per season. | points: points recorded on that driver_standings row (source: driver_standings.points). Not a season aggregate by itself — it's the points value as of that race snapshot. | position: standing position recorded on that driver_standings row (source: driver_standings.position). The position at that race snapshot. | rn: row number generated by ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ra.year, ds.driver_id ORDER BY ds.race_id DESC) (derived). rn = 1 indicates the latest available driver_standings row for that driver in that season.
params.grounded_columns: driver_standings.driver_standings_id | driver_standings.race_id | driver_standings.driver_id | driver_standings.points | driver_standings.position | races.race_id | races.year
params.metric: rn = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY races.year, driver_standings.driver_id ORDER BY driver_standings.race_id DESC) | points = driver_standings.points (snapshot metric, not aggregated over season) | position = driver_standings.position (snapshot attribute, not aggregated)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join to driver_dim on driver_id — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver (1:1 to this view's driver_id) and will not duplicate rows or measures. | Cardinality-safe: join to race_basic (or races) on race_id — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race; joining preserves this view's row-level uniqueness. | Do NOT join directly to race_results_w_driver_constructor, driver_lap_summary, pit_stops_per_driver, qualifying_grid_with_driver, or any other one-to-many facts without pre-aggregating those facts to the same grain (driver_standings_id or driver_id+year filtered to rn=1). Such joins will multiply this view's rows (one driver_standings row × many fact rows) and inflate measures like points. | If you need to combine with one-to-many facts, either: (a) aggregate the fact to one row per driver_standings_id (or per driver_id+year) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(...) GROUP BY driver_standings_id) — do not SUM directly after an un-aggregated join expecting original points to remain correct. | When joining to driver_season_points (an AGG sibling): ensure you understand which side holds the true season-aggregate. If driver_season_points already provides season-level totals, prefer joining on driver_id and year to that aggregated view instead of deriving totals by summing this view's points rows (unless you restrict rn=1).
params.comparison: use driver_season_points instead when you need season-level aggregated totals (e.g., total season points) — driver_season_points is an aggregate across the season and returns one row per driver-season rather than per race snapshot. | use race_basic when you need richer race attributes keyed by race_id — race_basic is normalized to race-level attributes and may be preferable to joining races directly. | use race_results_w_driver_constructor when you need per-race result details (finishing position, laps, fastest lap) — that view is one-to-many relative to this view and thus will expand rows; aggregate it first if combining with this view's rn=1 season snapshots. | use driver_running_points_by_season when you need cumulative running points across races within a season (running totals per race) — this view provides a single latest snapshot per season (when filtered to rn=1), whereas driver_running_points_by_season gives the progressive sequence.

views.description: Pick the latest available driver_standings row per year and driver based on race_id ordering. Exposes position and points as the most recent snapshot for that driver in the season. | Use for: Get final season standings (filter rn = 1 per year/driver); Compare mid-season vs final standings by selecting different rn values
